citeAs: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu (2025). Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation. arXiv:2510.20888.
creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu (ByteDance, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
description: VAP-Data is the largest dataset for semantic-controlled video generation, containing over 100K curated paired videos across 100 semantic conditions. It covers 4 primary categories — concept (entity transformation and interaction), style, motion (human and non-human), and camera movement — and was built by pairing 2K high-quality real reference images with visual-effects templates from commercial models and community LoRAs.
license: Research-only license with an acceptable-use policy (AUP) that explicitly prohibits abusive or unlawful scenarios
name: VAP-Data
rai:dataBiases: VAP-Data is synthetic and derived from other generative models (commercial APIs and community LoRAs), so it may inherit the specific stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of the source templates. For example, if the source models are poor at generating hands, VAP will likely not learn to generate hands well from this data. The semantic conditions are also relatively limited and synthetic compared to real-world data.
rai:dataCollection: The authors curated 2K high-quality real images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. They then used Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs to create paired videos by matching each image to all compatible templates (some restrict subject categories), resulting in over 100K paired samples across 100 semantic conditions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: 2K high-quality real images collected from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. These images were used as reference inputs to generate paired video data.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: VAP-Data has several limitations: (1) it is synthetic and derived from other generative models, inheriting their stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations; (2) the semantic conditions are relatively limited and synthetic; (3) building a large, real-world, semantic-controlled video dataset is left for future work; (4) performance depends on caption quality and structural similarity between subjects — it degrades when descriptions diverge or subjects differ markedly.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each reference image was matched to all compatible visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU, Kling) and community LoRAs to generate paired target videos. Some templates restrict subject categories, so not all images were paired with all templates. The dataset was split into training and test subsets; for evaluation, 24 semantic conditions were evenly sampled from 4 categories with 2 samples each (48 test samples total).
rai:dataSocialImpact: VAP targets semantic-controlled video generation for research, education, and creative prototyping. It is not intended for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments. Potential misuses include identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and generation of sexualized or violent media. Mitigations include a research-only release and default content filters blocking clearly harmful categories (e.g., sexual content, explicit violence, hate symbols).
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating unified semantic-controlled video generation models. Intended for research, education, and creative prototyping involving concept-guided, style-guided, motion-guided, and camera-guided video generation. Supports downstream applications including video stylization, motion imitation, camera control, and visual effects.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial Image-to-Video models VIDU and Kling (via their visual-effects APIs) and community LoRAs (from Civitai and other sources) were used to automatically generate paired target videos from reference images. Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-5 were used for automatic semantic-alignment scoring of generated videos.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images and videos of men, women, and children (human subjects), as well as content involving human faces and bodies (e.g., gender swap, hair color change, pet to human transformations). The paper notes misuse risks including identity impersonation and deepfake content generation.
